name: Antigua and Barbuda
summary: Antigua and Barbuda follows English common law, with no forced heirship found. It has an International Trust Act (2007) and private foundation legislation. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force for it.
foreign_law_note: No source read states Antigua's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate. Common-law rule: movables follow the law of the domicile, land follows local law. Not confirmed in local statute for this jurisdiction.
trust_note: Antigua is not in the HCCH status table. The International Trust Act 2007 (Act 18 of 2007) has sections on claims based on relationship and non-recognition of foreign judgments; a commercial guide says foreign forced-heirship judgments are not recognised. IFC Review lists Antigua among Caribbean states with private foundation laws; the Act's name was not confirmed.
open_questions: No source read confirms the absence of forced heirship or family provision claims in Antigua.
The foundation statute's name and text were not read.
Text of the 2007 Act's firewall sections not read.
